skill.name: brewpage-publish
skill.description: Publish text, Markdown, JSON, files, and static site archives to brewpage.app. The skill asks for namespace and password choices, uploads content, and returns a public URL.
skill.summary: Publish pages, files, JSON, and static sites to brewpage.app from Claude, Codex, or Claude Code.
skill.author: kochetkov-ma

security_audit.summary: Most static hits are Markdown formatting, documentation URLs, or protective exclusions rather than executable risk. Real issues remain in the Bash publish blocks, which interpolate user-controlled values before curl or zip execution and persist owner tokens in a workspace file.

remediation.issue: User-controlled values are interpolated into Bash snippets.
remediation.suggestion: Move publish logic into a reviewed script that accepts arguments through files or environment variables, validates namespace, TTL, and entry values, and avoids heredocs for user content.
Store owner tokens outside the project tree, set restrictive permissions, and add an explicit opt-in before saving tokens. At minimum, require .claude/brewpage-history.md in .gitignore.

remediation.issue: Pre-built ZIP archives bypass the directory exclusion list.
remediation.suggestion: Inspect ZIP contents before upload or rebuild ZIP archives from an allowlisted file list that excludes secrets, source maps, logs, dependencies, and VCS data.

remediation.issue: Uploads can create public links by default.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit confirmation for public publication of files and directories, and show the namespace, password state, TTL, and content summary before curl runs.

semantic_findings.title: Unescaped Shell Placeholder Interpolation
semantic_findings.description: The publish snippets interpolate user-controlled content, paths, namespace, TTL, and entry values into Bash commands before execution. Values containing heredoc delimiters, quotes, or command substitutions can change the generated command.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The Bash snippets place placeholders directly inside heredocs, single-quoted JSON, double-quoted URLs, cd commands, and multipart arguments. Those values come from user input or selected paths.

semantic_findings.title: Owner Tokens Persisted In Workspace History
semantic_findings.description: The skill creates .claude/brewpage-history.md and appends owner tokens beside public URLs. These tokens allow deletion of published pages and can be exposed through accidental commits or later file reads.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The file path and echo commands are explicit, and each publish path appends the owner token when present. The skill warns not to print tokens but still stores them locally.

semantic_findings.title: Pre-Built ZIP Upload Bypasses Secret Exclusions
semantic_findings.description: Directory uploads exclude common secret and project files, but the ZIP upload path sends the supplied archive as-is. A ZIP containing credentials, source maps, or repository data would be uploaded without the same filtering.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The SKILL.md instructions describe ZIP files as an alternative input and the ZIP publish block uploads archive=@{zip_file_path}. The exclusion list is only shown for the directory auto-zip path.

content.user_title: Publish Pages and Files to Brewpage
content.value_statement: Sharing small pages and files can require hosting setup. This skill publishes text, Markdown, JSON, files, or static sites to Brewpage and returns a URL.
actual_capabilities: Detects text, Markdown, JSON, single files, directories, and ZIP archives.
Publishes content to Brewpage HTML, JSON, file, and site endpoints.
Prompts for a namespace and optional password before publishing.
Generates a short random password with Bash when requested.
Auto-zips built static directories and excludes common secret and project files.
Saves owner tokens locally so published pages can be deleted later.
limitations: Requires Bash and command line tools such as curl, jq, zip, and file.
Uploads content to an external hosting service, often as a public link.
Pre-built ZIP archives are uploaded as-is and must be inspected first.
Owner tokens are stored in the workspace and must be protected.

use_cases.title: Share a Static Preview
use_cases.description: Publish a built site directory and send a temporary URL to reviewers.

use_cases.title: Publish a Draft Document
use_cases.description: Turn a Markdown note or report into a hosted page without setting up a server.

use_cases.title: Host a Data Sample
use_cases.description: Upload a JSON object or file and share a direct link for short-term collaboration.

prompt_templates.title: Publish a Note
prompt_templates.prompt: Publish this text to Brewpage with the default TTL. Ask me before using a public namespace or password.

prompt_templates.title: Share a Markdown File
prompt_templates.prompt: Publish report.md to Brewpage for 7 days. Use a descriptive namespace and ask me about password protection.

prompt_templates.title: Host a Built Site
prompt_templates.prompt: Publish the built site in ./dist with index.html as the entry file. Show the file count before upload and use a password.

prompt_templates.title: Publish With Cleanup
prompt_templates.prompt: Publish ./release-site as a Brewpage site for 3 days, confirm the archive excludes secrets, save the owner token, and summarize deletion steps.

output_examples.input: Publish a short Markdown announcement for 15 days.
output_examples.output: A Brewpage URL is returned, with the owner token saved locally instead of shown in chat.

output_examples.input: Upload ./dist as a site with a password.
output: The skill reports the selected entry file and file count.
It returns the site URL and notes that the owner token was saved.

output_examples.input: Share a JSON status document for one day.
output_examples.output: The skill posts the JSON to Brewpage and returns a temporary link for sharing.

best_practices: Inspect files and directories before publishing them to Brewpage.
Use password protection for drafts, private files, and review links.
Protect the owner-token history file and keep it out of version control.
anti_patterns: Publishing source trees instead of built static output.
Uploading ZIP archives that have not been checked for secrets.
Sharing owner tokens or committing the history file.

faq.question: What can this skill publish?
faq.answer: It can publish text, Markdown, JSON, single files, directories, and ZIP archives to Brewpage.

faq.question: Does it require a Brewpage account?
faq.answer: The README states that no sign-up is required for publishing.

faq.question: Is published content public?
faq.answer: By default, content can be public. Use password protection when the content is private or unfinished.

faq.question: Where are owner tokens stored?
faq.answer: The skill saves owner tokens in .claude/brewpage-history.md so users can delete published pages later.

faq.question: What command line tools are needed?
faq.answer: The skill uses Bash with tools such as curl, jq, zip, tr, head, mktemp, and file.

faq.question: How should ZIP uploads be handled?
faq.answer: Inspect ZIP archives before upload because pre-built ZIP files are sent as-is.
